title: Canary-lane siphon and cost containment pipeline for safe production duplication
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a production-safe traffic siphon ("canary-lane") that routes a deterministically sampled subset of live requests to a sandboxed inference sink for canary/AB/validation purposes while enforcing tenant-level cost limits and strict isolation. The goal is to enable continuous validation of model variants without exposing user-facing latency or incurring uncontrolled spend. This ticket covers routing logic, sampling policy, tenant budgeting, sandbox sink hardening, metrics, and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Live requests can be duplicated to a sandbox sink using the canary-lane without adding measurable latency to the primary path (<= 5ms p95 overhead).
Per-tenant sampling probability can be configured and dynamically adjusted via runtime policy with immediate effect.
Sandbox sink is network-isolated and does not write to production logs or downstream systems by default.
Cost-controller enforces monthly and ephemeral credit limits per tenant and prevents duplication when a tenant is above budget.
Automated rollback triggers: if canary error-rate delta > 3x baseline or prompt-eval quality regression > 5% on monitored prompt set, duplication is disabled and on-call is paged.
Dashboard exposes duplication volume, per-tenant credit burn, sample entropy, and queue/backpressure indicators.
End-to-end integration tests simulate tenant budget exhaustion, sampler ramp-up, and failover to fallback model with correct auditing entries.
Design doc and migration plan reviewed and approved by security and platform infra teams.
tasks: Design routing shim (canary-lane) that attaches a duplication token to a request and forks it to the sandbox sink asynchronously
Implement dynamic sampling service: supports static probability, credit-based depletion, and 'burst' policy for short-term investigative ramps
Build tenant-budget controller: integrates with billing/credits API, emits denial reason, and exposes 'grace' window behavior
Harden sandbox sink: KV cache isolation, no write-through to telemetry except aggregated counters, and HSM/KMS constraints for any sensitive payloads
Create circuit-breaker that disables duplication for a tenant on thresholds (error delta, latency spike, cost burn), with cooldown and audit trail
Add per-request metadata tagging for traceability and cost accounting (tenant, route, sampler-version, credit-consumed)
Instrument dashboards and alerts: duplication QPS, duplicated token latency, per-tenant spend rate, sampler entropy, rollback events
Author e2e tests and chaos scenarios for partial network partition and sandbox outage behavior
Write runbook: how to manually disable siphon globally, per-tenant, and how to re-enable after investigation

decisions: Sandbox sink will run in a tenant-isolated network namespace with no external write permissions by default.
Use probabilistic sampling plus credit tokens (hybrid approach) to give tenants predictable exposure while letting product teams do short bursts for debugging.
Duplicate requests will bypass production KV cache unless explicitly whitelisted to avoid polluting cache accounting and to measure model behavior on cold starts.
Rollback is automated: duplication disabled immediately when thresholds are crossed; manual review required before reopen.
